# W007 — compressed algebraic norms with distinct roots

2026-10-08. Parent-led fresh branch. PROVISIONAL; no factoring improvement,
candidate execution, new benchmark, or Lean theorem. The question is whether
a norm polynomial with exponentially many DISTINCT useful local roots can be
constructed and evaluated with only polynomially many bit operations.

This replaces relation collection and random group collision generation with
a direct gcd(N,P(x)) test for a succinctly specified polynomial. Both useful
root coverage and the construction of P are charged. A degree bound alone
is never a lower bound on root count.

## Candidate A: anti-commuting block norms — explicit rejection

Let A_1=[[0,t_1],[t_1,0]], and recursively

    A_(j+1) = [[A_j,t_(j+1) I],[t_(j+1) I,-A_j]].

The dimension is 2^j but A_j^2=S_j I, S_j=sum_(i<=j) t_i^2, and trace A_j=0.
Over characteristic zero,

    det(X I-A_j)=(X^2-S_j)^(2^(j-1)).

As an integer polynomial identity it survives reduction modulo any N.
Compute S_j and the displayed power by modular arithmetic without building
the matrix. This really eliminates an exponential determinant, but it leaves
at most two distinct roots over each odd prime. Singular reductions may have
one root, not more. A proper gcd of the huge determinant is already explained
by gcd(X^2-S_j,N); repeated-prime valuations need their own capped treatment.
The exponential degree is only multiplicity. This exact computation therefore
does not provide a root-density gain.

A commuting tensor sum instead has roots sum_i epsilon_i t_i. Repeated or
few distinct weights can again create large multiplicities. Superincreasing
weights give many distinct roots but the obvious norm evaluation enumerates
them; the binary-weight example becomes a large arithmetic-progression product.
The old H029/H030 product gates are not waived by calling that product a norm.

## Candidate B: a concrete nested split polynomial — selected

Set P_0(X)=X and define

    P_(j+1)(X)=P_j(X)*(P_j(X)-a_j).

A supplied list a_0,...,a_(j-1) gives an actual O(j)-operation modular evaluator
for a monic polynomial of degree 2^j. It is also the norm of X-T in the
algebra (Z/NZ)[T]/P_j(T), but no dense basis or general norm routine is used.
This particular recurrence performs the evaluation.

The adaptive construction chooses a_j=P_j(r_j) for an explicitly obtained
rational r_j, so the new polynomial retains old roots and adds that fiber.
Evaluating all training values naively costs O(j^2) modular operations.
There are no hidden p,q or local orders in this program. Every denominator
is gcd-tested before inversion; a proper gcd is an early factor, a full gcd
is an exhausted parameter attempt. Neither raw rational height nor formal
degree is automatically the cost: an explicitly short modular arithmetic
circuit can avoid expanding large integers. Its circuit construction,
constants, denominator branches and reduced operand widths still must be paid.

An actual three-stage split construction is

    a_0=1,  a_1=2,  a_2=-504/625,
    P_1=X(X-1),
    P_2=X(X-1)(X-2)(X+1),
    P_3=P_2*(P_2+504/625).

P_2(-4/5)=-504/625, and

    P_2+504/625
      =(X+4/5)(X-9/5)(X+2/5)(X-7/5).

Thus P_3 has eight distinct rational roots
{-1,0,1,2,-4/5,9/5,-2/5,7/5}. For primes p>13 their denominators are units and
their residues remain distinct (all pairwise numerator differences have
absolute value at most 15). This gives exactly eight roots modulo those primes.
It is a concrete finite construction, not evidence of an all-depth generator.

By contrast, the obvious r_2=3 gives a_2=24 and

    P_2-24=(X-3)(X+2)(X^2-X+4).

Only six rational roots of P_3 are then automatic; the remaining quadratic
has discriminant -15. This explicitly refutes automatic rational root doubling.

For an odd squarefree N=pq, conditional on a fixed eligible polynomial and
a uniform x modulo N, if its local zero fractions are z_p,z_q, then the
proper-gcd probability is z_p(1-z_q)+z_q(1-z_p). A full gcd is not a factor.
At the displayed fixed degree this is only a constant number of ordinary
root tests. A disruptive consequence would require a PAID scalable construction
with many distinct roots modulo unknown input primes and a separating
success law. No such construction has been established.

## Exact next gate: obtaining the fourth fully split fiber

Keep this P_3 fixed. To retain sixteen distinct rational roots via the same
recurrence, obtain a nonzero rational a_3 such that P_3(X)-a_3 splits into
eight distinct rational roots. Its roots are disjoint from P_3(X)=0 when
a_3 is nonzero. The known a_3=0 is a duplicate, not progress.

The degree-eight cover P_3(X)->T has the following proposed finite branch
values, obtained at the three levels' critical points:

    b_2=-63504/390625,
    b_1=121/625,
    b_0=123201/160000.

They are distinct. Proposed inertia orders are 2,2,2 at these values and
8 at infinity. A plausible full geometric Galois group is the three-level
binary wreath product, of order 128. IF that group and ramification audit
is correct, its Galois closure has

    2g-2 = 128*(-2+3*(1-1/2)+(1-1/8))=48,  hence g=25.

This genus is NOT yet accepted. The reviewer must prove the actual group,
constant field, ramification and relation between completely split rational
fibers and rational points, or correct the proposed conclusion. A positive
genus alone is not an algorithmic lower bound, and genus 25 does not prove
there is no additional split fiber. It would invalidate a presumed rational
one-parameter parametrization of the fixed cover's full splitting data.
It does not exclude varying earlier coefficients or working only over F_p.

circle construction for a completely split fiber; blindly extending that
parametrization to degree eight may fail for a specific geometric reason.
Do not launch an unbounded rational-point search or assume a point oracle.
A finite symbolic group/branch audit is selected first.

This uses the same evaluator but a different acquisition rule: r_j is a
fresh uniform residue modulo N and a_j=P_j(r_j). Over one prime, fix the
current P_j and let mu(y)=Pr_x[P_j(x)=y], z=mu(0), c=sum_y mu(y)^2.
The fresh a_j has law mu. For a fixed a, the new zero fraction is

    z'=z+mu(a)-1_(a=0)*z,

and therefore E[z'-z | P_j]=c-z^2.
This is an actual size-biased fiber addition, not an assumed concentration
oracle. For the collision probability of the full next distribution, the
quadratic identity y(y-a)=w(w-a) iff y=w or y+w=a suggests exactly

    c'(a)=c+sum_y mu(y)*mu(a-y)-mu(a/2)^2.

global stopping, no exponential growth model and no complete factor bound

NEW EXCLUSIVE NOTE:
# W007 — varying earlier coefficients instead of searching one fixed fiber

2026-10-08. Parent constructive continuation. PROVISIONAL; independent task A
audits only the original fixed degree-eight cover and basic laws. This note
changes the acquisition computation and must not be claimed as part of A's
completed work. No numerical search or new factoring bound.

## An explicit joint construction condition

Keep P_2(X)=X(X-1)(X-2)(X+1). Define the rational split-value set S by

    t in S iff P_2(X)-t has four distinct rational roots.

Writing s^2=1+t, complete splitting is equivalent to rational A,B with

    A^2=5+4s, B^2=5-4s, hence A^2+B^2=10,

with the repeated-root exceptional values removed. Conversely every such
circle point gives t=((A^2-B^2)/8)^2-1. The circle has the rational
parametrization obtained by rotating (1,3):

    A=(1-u^2-6u)/(1+u^2),
    B=(3-3u^2+2u)/(1+u^2).

This is a paid constant-size rational computation, not a rational-point oracle.

Instead of fixing a_2=-504/625 and searching one fiber of that P_3, choose
three members t_1,t_2,t_3 of S satisfying

    t_1+t_2=t_3.

Require t_1,t_2,t_3 nonzero, t_1!=t_2, and all four fibers at
0,t_1,t_2,t_3 simple. Nonzero t_1,t_2 and t_1+t_2=t_3 already make those four
values distinct once t_3!=0 and t_1!=t_2. Set

    a_2=t_3,   a_3=-t_1*t_2,
    P_3=P_2*(P_2-t_3),
    P_4=P_3*(P_3+t_1*t_2).

Then the exact identity

    P_3+t_1*t_2=(P_2-t_1)*(P_2-t_2)

makes P_4 the product of FOUR disjoint completely split quartic fibers:
P_2, P_2-t_1, P_2-t_2, P_2-t_3. It therefore has sixteen distinct rational
roots and a four-stage evaluator. This is an explicit sufficient AND, for
this particular nested shape with fully split intermediate fibers, necessary
condition. The existence/acquisition of a nontrivial additive triple is not
asserted. t_1=0, t_2=0, t_1=t_2 and t_3=0 are not acceptable shortcuts.

The fixed genus proposed in the original brief would not by itself obstruct
this varying-a_2 construction. Conversely, replacing a fixed curve by a
higher-dimensional equation does not supply a point or a scalable algorithm.

## Connection to a concrete primary-literature construction

If two monic degree-d polynomials split over Q and differ by a nonzero
constant, their root lists have equal power sums through degree d-1, by
Newton identities. Conversely such equal power sums force equality of all
nonconstant coefficients. Thus each completely split new fiber is an
ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott pair after clearing denominators. This is an
elementary equivalence, not a new result.

A primary paper to inspect is Ajai Choudhry, "Ideal solutions of the
Tarry-Escott Problem of degree seven", arXiv:2207.12726. Its abstract reports
parametric ideal size-eight solutions; the parent has NOT inspected its
formulas or claimed they give this nested construction. A second bounded
source is Coppersmith–Mossinghoff–Scheinerman–VanderKam,
"Ideal solutions in the Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem", arXiv:2304.11254.
Do not infer a uniform all-size construction from their finite sizes.

There is a precise compatibility test for using a symmetric size-eight pair.
Translate the common root center to zero. Write the first even polynomial as

    Q(Y)=Y^4+B Y^3+C Y^2+D Y+E,   with Y=X^2.

It is a composition of two monic quadratics exactly when

    D=(B/2)*(C-B^2/4).

Indeed expanding (Y^2+uY+v)^2+w(Y^2+uY+v)+z gives B=2u and
D=u(C-u^2); conversely v can be chosen and w,z recovered.
A general ideal size-eight pair need not satisfy this condition. The second
quartic has the same B,C,D and therefore satisfies it whenever the first does.

Equivalently, the four squared positive-half roots admit a pairing with
equal pair sums. If x_1^2+x_2^2=x_3^2+x_4^2=H and the y-half roots have the
same property, their second-power sums already agree. Matching fourth-power
sums also matches sixth-power sums, since for x^2+y^2=H,

    x^4+y^4=H^2-2x^2*y^2,
    x^6+y^6=H^3-3H*x^2*y^2.

This reduces the symmetric ideal constraints to matching sums of two
squared coordinate products while maintaining rational circle points.
It is a more specific construction target than "find an ideal PTE solution".

A bounded source-and-algebra audit should decide whether a published
parametric family satisfies, or can explicitly be specialized to, this extra
composition condition without collapsing the two root sets. If so, give the
actual coefficients and denominator/degeneracy conditions. If not, identify
the additional equation instead of claiming that PTE prior art solves it.
Either outcome is still a finite-stage result, not scalable factoring.

## Costs and what would change the research conclusion

If an explicit rational additive triple or compatible published family is
obtained, its coefficient circuit can be reduced modulo N after gcd-testing
denominators. No list of sixteen roots is needed to evaluate P_4, although
root distinctness modulo an unknown p still needs proof or exception handling.
For general depth, useful local coverage, noncollapsed roots, circuit size,
coefficient acquisition and a separating factor law all remain required.
Finite degree-eight/sixteen formulas are a way to test actual algebraic growth,
not evidence of polynomial-time factoring or an improvement over NFS.

No experiment is authorized here. In particular do not replace this gate by
a broad rational-height sweep whose growing search cost is hidden.

- **No lowest terms needed.** Any integers u_j, v_j with v_j ≠ 0 work. Then A_j = D_j·P_j lies in Z[X] with degree exactly 2^j and leading coefficient D_j. Every rational root of A_k has a denominator dividing D_k.

- **Exact cost, with constants built from 1 only:** tau(H_k) ≤ 8k + T. That is 2 operations per stage for the D_j, 6 per stage for the homogeneous recurrence, and T for building the constants.
- **Adaptive constants a_j = P_j(r_j), r_j = m_j/n_j:** take u_j = A_j^h(m_j, n_j) and v_j = D_j·n_j^(2^j). Then tau(H_k) ≤ 3k² + 11k + Σ[tau(|m_j|) + tau(n_j)]. This matches the parent's Θ(k²) training cost, so nothing is hidden.

- **Constants with paid division-free programs, or polynomial-size binary:** if the root count is superpolynomial in 8k + T, H_k refutes the tau conjecture. - **Lipton 1994:** only the abstract was reachable; Springer blocked the full text. I did not rely on its hypotheses.

- Rojas's p-adic bounds already allow about p·e^(s log s) roots, so they don't limit root density mod p.
